items.title: Red Tape Theory™: Just Because We Can Does Not Mean We Should — A Study of Generative AI, Creative Utility, and Brand Appropriateness
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence has rapidly reduced the distance between imagining a creative artifact and producing it. Images, videos, written works, advertisements, illustrations, and other forms of media that once required substantial time, labor, technical expertise, or financial resources can now be generated with comparatively little production effort. This paper examines the distinction between whether something can be produced and whether producing it is appropriate, useful, accurate, relevant, or communicatively successful. Using the framework of Red Tape Theory™, the paper investigates the proposition: Just because we can does not mean we should. The proposition is not presented as an argument against artificial intelligence, generative media, or technological experimentation. Rather, it examines the possibility that increased technological capability can create a tendency to treat capability itself as justification for use. The paper develops a series of distinctions: CAPABILITY ≠ APPROPRIATENESSNOVELTY ≠ VALUETECHNICAL QUALITY ≠ COMMUNICATIVE SUCCESSBEAUTY ≠ ACCURACYATTENTION ≠ UNDERSTANDINGPRODUCTION EFFICIENCY ≠ CREATIVE JUSTIFICATIONCAN ≠ SHOULD Three observational contexts are examined. First, the author’s use of generative AI across different creative tasks demonstrates the importance of task-dependent utility and tool selection. OpenAI systems have been used for conceptual development, thesis writing, philosophical exploration, poetry, and children’s literature, while other generative systems have been used for more straightforward visual-production tasks. This comparison is presented not as a universal ranking of AI systems, but as an example of a tool-agnostic, purpose-first approach to creative technology. Second, publicly documented NFL–Adobe implementations of generative AI are examined as an example of AI being incorporated into a large-scale brand and content ecosystem. The case illustrates how generative technology can be used for content scaling, personalization, workflow efficiency, governance, and brand-oriented production while simultaneously raising questions about the relationship between technical possibility and communicative relevance. Third, the paper examines brand appropriateness and the possibility that an artifact may be technically sophisticated while remaining poorly aligned with the identity, purpose, audience, or context for which it was created. The paper proposes that creative evaluation should distinguish at least five dimensions: Capability — Can the system produce the requested artifact?Accuracy — Does the artifact correctly represent its subject?Quality — Is the artifact technically and aesthetically successful?Relevance — Does it serve the communication objective?Appropriateness — Does it belong within the brand and audience context? These dimensions should not be collapsed into a single judgment of whether an artifact is simply “good.” Within Red Tape Theory™, the resulting decision process is: PURPOSE → AUDIENCE → IDEA → TOOL → OUTPUT → OBSERVATION → QUESTION → ADJUSTMENT rather than: CAPABILITY → FIND SOMETHING TO USE IT FOR The paper further examines the consequences of reduced production friction. When generative systems make experimentation inexpensive, the number of possible creative artifacts can expand faster than the human capacity to evaluate them. The resulting abundance may increase the importance of creative judgment, taste, selection, restraint, and purpose rather than eliminate the need for them. The central argument is therefore not that AI should or should not be used. It is that technological capability does not independently establish creative justification. A system may produce something extraordinary without that extraordinary artifact being appropriate to the task. A generated image may be beautiful while inaccurately representing a product.A video may be technically impressive while confusing its audience.A campaign may generate enormous quantities of content while weakening the identity it was intended to reinforce.A novel visual concept may attract attention without communicating its intended meaning. The relevant question is consequently not simply: “What can this technology do?” but: “What are we trying to accomplish, and does this technology help us accomplish it?” Red Tape Theory™ treats these conditions as an observation problem rather than an automatic verdict. Audience discomfort does not by itself prove creative failure, just as technical sophistication does not by itself prove creative success. The relationship between purpose, artifact, audience response, and interpretation must remain open to investigation. The paper concludes that as production becomes easier, creative judgment becomes more important rather than less important. The technology can create the possibility. The human must still determine whether the possibility serves the purpose. YOU CANNOT FORCE AN AXIOM.™

items.title: Referential Uncertainty in Human--AI Collaboration
items.abstract: Effective human-AI collaboration requires partners to establish references through interaction, which becomes fragile when descriptions are ambiguous, similar referents compete, or partners see different things. We study referential uncertainty - uncertainty over which candidate object a description refers to - in a collaborative puzzle task where a human Helper instructs an AI Worker to place pieces. The Worker must identify and communicate its uncertainty, and the Helper must recognize and act on it. We show that a separately elicited belief distribution over candidate pieces is better calibrated (ECE 0.15) and better discriminates correct from incorrect placements (AUROC 0.65) than raw action-token probabilities, which are severely overconfident (0.97 mean confidence, ECE 0.44). Across three frontier vision-language models (GPT-4.1, GPT-5, GPT-5.5), this elicited uncertainty rises predictably with instruction vagueness, but not with competing referents in context, even when those increase errors. The models seldom externalize it, asking for clarification on only 3.5-16.7% of turns. In a controlled human study (N=210), participants given only the Worker's default message accept 78% of wrong placements and cannot tell right from wrong (AUC 0.50). Precise descriptions and, especially, well-targeted hedges cut wrong-move acceptance to 36% while largely preserving correct-move acceptance, compensating for missing shared awareness such as not seeing the Worker's action. But this benefit depends on targeting: a deployable hedge derived from the model's own belief entropy inherits that signal's weakness and can do more harm than good. Externalized uncertainty helps a human partner only when it is accurately targeted.

items.title: Representation of Artificial Intelligence in Contemporary Fiction
items.abstract: Abstract: The present research paper deals with the representation of artificial intelligence in the contemporary fiction. The rapid developments of artificial intelligence had generated corresponding proliferation of literary narratives concerned with intelligent machines, artificial consciousness, automation, human-machine intimacy and the boundaries of human world. While earlier science fiction often imagined intelligent machines primarily as either servants or threats; recent literature presents artificial intelligence in more complex roles such as companion, worker, friend, moral agent and political subject. Such representations make the distinction between human and machines very complex and redefine the concepts like consciousness, emotion, autonomy and responsibility. Hence, in this paper an attempt is made to take the review of AI reflected in the contemporary fiction. Keywords: artificial intelligence, contemporary fiction, science fiction, human-machine relationships, technology identity.

items.title: Rethinking Student Assignments in Higher Education in the Age of Generative AI: From Product Assessment to Process-Oriented Learning
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) can contribute to idea generation, content organisation, language editing, and product revision, making it difficult for teachers to judge students’ knowledge and understanding, cognitive engagement, and independent contribution solely from the final assignment. This study employed a focused integrative literature review and conducted structured extraction, source-type appraisal, thematic coding, and cross-text comparison across 37 materials: 24 GenAI-related studies, eight classic works on assessment theory, and five policy and guidance documents. The findings indicate that final products remain valuable for assessing students’ overall performance, but their explanatory power as a single source of learning evidence has diminished under conditions of human-AI co-production. Drawing on the literature synthesis, this article proposes a six-stage process-oriented assignment framework comprising task interpretation, independent attempt, human-AI interaction, information verification, outcome revision, and reflective disclosure. The framework is guided by alignment with learning outcomes, student agency, visibility of cognitive engagement, transparency and responsibility, and proportionality. It links sustainable assessment with long-term evaluative capability, responsible AI use, equitable participation, and manageable evidence requirements. As a literature-informed conceptual proposal, its effectiveness, scope of application, and implementation burden require examination across disciplines and course contexts.

items.title: Scalable decision-making for games of imperfect information
items.abstract: Abstract Real-world decision-making generally involves hidden information, that is, information that is unknown to one agent but possessed by another. Unfortunately, the presence of large amounts of hidden information renders established reinforcement learning and search approaches ineffective. Even with multimillion-dollar industrial research efforts 1 , top-human-level play at Stratego—a board wargame with hidden information on a massive scale—has remained beyond the reach of artificial intelligence (AI). Here we introduce Ataraxos, an AI for Stratego based on general techniques that we developed for both self-play reinforcement learning and test-time search under hidden information. Ataraxos defeated the most decorated human Stratego player of all time by a large margin—achieving, to our knowledge, the first superhuman result in the game’s history—while consuming orders of magnitude less compute and data than previous efforts. Using the same techniques, we built a superhuman AI for Barrage Stratego and state-of-the-art AIs for Hanabi and dou dizhu , all with low cost and high sample efficiency. The success of this approach across adversarial, cooperative and team games establishes a design pattern for reinforcement learning and search that is effective under large amounts of hidden information, a longstanding desideratum of the field of strategic decision-making.

items.title: Schema: Discovering Unknown Environments via Agentic Program Induction
items.abstract: Learning to complete tasks in unfamiliar environments with unknown rules remains a key challenge for LLM agents. Current LLM agents often record their discoveries in prose, which may not provide a compact, explicit account of how the environment works. Inspired by how scientists organize observations into testable, predictive theories, we introduce Schema, an agent harness that organizes learning and action through interactive program induction. The LLM agent decides what to investigate and how to act, expressing its evolving understanding of the environment as executable programs. The harness consists of a persistent program workspace and a small set of interfaces for checking these programs against the interaction history, planning within them, and executing plans under step-by-step verification. Schema raises ARC-AGI-3 RHAE from 58.7% to 99.2% with the same base model, solves 100% of the public DiG-bench games, and reaches the median performance of the top-50 human players on MazeBench. Extensive analysis shows the effectiveness of Schema in unknown mechanism discovery, and ablations confirm the contribution of each component.

items.title: Seamful Design Considerations for Human-in-the-Loop Digital Phenotyping of Mental Health
items.abstract: Digital Phenotyping of Mental Health (DPMH) through passive sensing is a promising approach for personal health informatics and digital wellbeing. Its appeal lies in unobtrusiveness, making it appear seamless. However, this very quality leads users to find it impersonal, untrustworthy, and disengaging. To counteract challenges of seamlessness, researchers propose seamful design to deliberately engage users. Yet, it remains unclear how this principle can be incorporated into digital phenotyping. To address this, we conducted a formative study by developing DYMOND. It is a technology probe that estimates depression, explains estimates, reveals discrepancies, and provides user control over the underlying model. In a 6-week deployment, 22 individuals with moderate-severe depression monitored their state with DYMOND. They interviewed every two weeks with researchers to collaboratively reconfigure the model and co-design new interfaces. Our analysis of 57 sessions revealed (i) seams—friction points—across data, modeling, and output, and (ii) design requirements helping users evaluate and mitigate seams. These findings inform the design requirements for human-in-the-loop DPMH to support agency, transparency, and collaborative reflection. This study provides insight into theoretical re-conceptualization for passive sensing, opportunities to integrate large language models and human-AI interaction for better interfaces for digital mental health, and pathways to involve expert stakeholders in DPMH.

items.title: Searching for a New Standard for Fair Artificial Intelligence: Feminist Artificial Intelligence Gender Bias Evaluation Framework
items.abstract: This study addresses the problem of algorithmic gender bias, which has become increasingly visible in artificial intelligence systems, and presents a feminist audit framework for this problem. Aiming to strengthen the interaction between technical audit mechanisms and feminist theoretical frameworks, this research has developed the Feminist Artificial Intelligence Gender Bias Evaluation Framework (FemAI-DEC), which brings theoretical knowledge together with an applicable evaluation practice. Structured in light of feminist theoretical approaches, this model includes four main dimensions: Data Justice, Design and Participation, Output Analysis, and Accountability and Transparency. This framework has been made available in a digital environment through an interactive scoring system in order to enable the systematic auditing of AI systems, make ethical risks measurable, and increase transparency. This digital tool, as a conceptual development study, aims to provide a concrete contribution to both academic discussions and the development of inclusive AI policies with its accessible structure that does not require technical expertise.

items.title: SHARPO: Segment-Level Credit Assignment for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
items.abstract: Agentic reinforcement learning (RL) trains a large language model (LLM) to act over long, multi-step interactions. However, a single localized error can cause task failure, while trajectory-level rewards provide limited guidance for assigning credit to individual decisions. To address this limitation, we introduce Segment-level Hindsight Advantage Reweighting for Policy Optimization (SHARPO), a credit-assignment mechanism that refines Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) at the level of environment-facing segments. Inspired by the existing on-policy self-distillation (OPSD) method, SHARPO computes teacher-student log-probability gaps within each segment and uses the resulting signal to compute a bounded multiplier on the GRPO advantage. This multiplier is shared by all tokens within the segment, allowing credit to vary across different segments. With Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, SHARPO outperforms existing baselines on the ALFWorld and WebShop benchmarks, including GRPO, SDAR, RLSD, and StepOPSD.

items.title: Skill-Based AI Agents for Power-System Studies
items.abstract: This paper describes a skill-based agentic framework for power-system studies using Model Context Protocol (MCP)-connected engineering tools. A custom MCP server was developed to expose Siemens PTI PSSE functions for power-flow analysis, dynamic simulation, result extraction, and model-validation workflows. Two implementation pathways built on a programmable OpenAI Agents software development kit (SDK) and a Claude Code command-line interface (CLI) were evaluated, both using reusable skills, subagents, MCP tools, data-repository connections, and local shell/Python execution. Both frontier-model-based implementations successfully executed representative study tasks. Success was evaluated based on task completion, output accuracy, and the need for human expert interventions. Results based on public datasets show that agentic systems can greatly accelerate power system dynamic simulation process for transmission planning studies leveraging industry-grade simulation platforms. This points toward a shift in transmission planning practice, where agentic systems could handle routine simulation setup and result extraction, allowing engineers to focus expert judgment on scenario design and interpretation rather than tool operation.

items.title: STRATA: Self-Learning Through Role-Aligned Tiered Agents for Real-Time Strategy Games
items.abstract: Real-time strategy (RTS) games require agents to coordinate economic development, production and construction, base defense, unit organization, and attack timing over long matches. Existing studies have applied large language models to command decision-making in RTS games, enabling agents to read textual game states and generate high-level plans. However, long inference latency can cause them to miss critical tactical events. The complexity and tactical diversity of full RTS matches also leave existing systems heavily dependent on manually written experience-based prompts, with limited ability to learn continuously from past games. We present STRATA, a role-aligned hierarchical system with cross-game self-learning for Red Alert. STRATA assigns in-game strategic, logistical, and tactical decisions to a Strategic Agent (SA), Logistics Agent (LA), and Tactical Agent (TA), respectively. The SA generates high-level directives based on the global game state and relevant experience cards, while the LA and TA handle logistics and tactical execution. After each match, a Review Agent (RA) derives candidate experience from game traces, validates and revises it using evidence from subsequent matches, and compresses strategic experience supported across multiple games into concise experience cards for SA retrieval. We evaluate STRATA through the formation of experience cards, full-match comparisons before and after learning, and experience learning against AI opponents with different play styles. Under a fixed scenario, using the learned experience cards increases the observed win rate from 30% to 100%. Sequential learning against AI opponents with different play styles also produces distinct long-term strategic experience.

items.title: STUDI PENERAPAN K3 DI LINGKUNGAN PRODUCTION PLANT-1 PT MULTI NITROTAMA
items.abstract: The chemical industry is associated with high occupational risks due to hazardous chemicals, pressurized equipment, and complex production processes. Therefore, the implementation of Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) is essential to prevent workplace accidents and support sustainable industrial operations. This study aims to evaluate the implementation of OHS in the Production Plant-1 environment of PT Multi Nitrotama Kimia and identify areas requiring improvement. A descriptive qualitative approach was employed using primary and secondary data collected through direct observation, interviews, documentation studies, and analysis of the company’s I’m Safe program records. Data were processed through reduction, classification, tabulation, and presentation to assess OHS practices comprehensively. The findings show that workers consistently comply with Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) requirements and that emergency preparedness systems, including fire extinguishers, evacuation routes, Emergency Response Teams (ERT), and safety training programs, have been implemented effectively. However, deficiencies were identified in pipeline identification and safety signage systems. Most production pipelines lacked flow direction markers, and several work areas were not adequately equipped with safety signs. In addition, inconsistencies were observed in Pre-Start Briefing implementation and procedural compliance despite high participation in the I’m Safe program. As an improvement measure, flow direction markers were installed on production pipelines. Overall, PT Multi Nitrotama Kimia has demonstrated a strong commitment to OHSMS implementation, although improvements in hazard communication, risk control, and procedural consistency remain necessary. items.title: Sustainability motivation and subjective well-being: an investigation of customer citizenship behavior in online food delivery in Vietnam
items.abstract: This research explores the relationship between consumers' sustainability motivation and their subjective well-being. Drawing on Self-Determination Theory and value co-creation literature, this study examines how intrinsic motivation affects the positive psychological outcome in online food delivery services. Observations were gathered from 298 Vietnamese consumers who used to order food via mobile applications, and then applied Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) to analyze data. The findings confirmed that sustainability motivation significantly positively influences customer citizenship behavior. And, perceived contribution to others' welfare was found to positively affect subjective well-being, validating its mediating role in the relationship between customer citizenship behavior and subjective well-being. In addition, platform trust moderates the relationship between customer citizenship behavior and perceived contribution to others' welfare, highlighting its importance in fostering prosocial behaviors within the platform. These results extend value co-creation theory by explaining how intrinsic motivation is transformed into customer behaviors and heightened subjective well-being in digital platforms. These outcomes offer practical directions for platform managers who have been seeking to build trust, enhance transparency, and feature users’ positive contributions to encourage responsible engagement and long-term value co-creation.

items.title: Task Source Matters: Eye‐Tracking Evidence on Cognitive Load and Decision Accuracy in ICU Multitasking
items.abstract: AIM: To examine how task source and disease severity influence cognitive workload and decision-making performance among intensive care unit nurses during concurrent multitasking. Understanding how different clinical information sources influence nurses' decision-making may provide insights for supporting decision-making in complex critical care environments. DESIGN: A laboratory-based 2 × 2 mixed-design experimental study. METHODS: Thirty ICU nurses participated in a concurrent task prioritization task in which task source (machine-induced vs. human-induced) and disease severity (high vs. low) were manipulated. Eye-tracking measures, including fixation, saccade, blink, and pupil diameter metrics, together with decision accuracy, were collected during 80 task trials per participant. RESULTS: Decision accuracy was significantly higher for machine-induced tasks than for human-induced tasks and was also higher under high-severity conditions than under low-severity conditions. Significant main effects of task source were observed across multiple eye-tracking measures. Compared with human-induced tasks, machine-induced tasks were associated with higher cognitive workload, reflected by increased total fixation duration, fixation count, saccade count, and pupil diameter. Disease severity significantly affected several eye-tracking measures; however, these effects were mainly observed during human-induced tasks, with no significant severity-related differences during machine-induced tasks. CONCLUSION: Task source and disease severity influence cognitive processing patterns during ICU multitasking. Higher cognitive workload does not necessarily impair clinical decision accuracy, and task-related information characteristics play a critical role in shaping decision-making performance. IMPLICATIONS FOR THE PROFESSION: The findings highlight the need for nursing practice to consider how different sources of task demands shape cognitive processing during multitasking. Recognizing that higher cognitive workload may support accurate decision-making under certain information conditions can inform task prioritization, clinical training, and the cognition-sensitive decision support for ICU nurses. IMPACT: This work advances evidence-based understanding of cognitive workload and decision-making in intensive care nursing. PATIENT OR PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION: No patient or public contribution.

items.title: Teacher Autonomy Support and Learning Engagement in Flipped Classroom Method: The Mediating Roles of Intrinsic Motivation and Self-Regulated Learning
items.abstract: As the adoption of flipped classroom methods (FCM) continues to grow in higher education, understanding the factors that promote students' learning engagement is crucial. While teachers' autonomy support (TAS) is widely recognized to enhance it, the underlying mechanism remains largely unexplored within the context. Based on Self-Determination Theory (SDT) and Constructivist Learning Theory, the study examined the mediating effects of students' intrinsic motivation (IM) and self-regulated learning (SRL) between TAS and learning engagement in a cross-sectional research design. Data were collected from 360 university students across six Indian states, and mediation analysis was incorporated. The findings disclosed that TAS positively impacts the learning engagement of the students directly and indirectly by fostering IM and SRL. It supports the propositions of the two theories. It suggests that autonomy-supportive pedagogical practices fashion psychologically empowering learning environments that, in turn, encourage learners to actively participate, thus creating effective student-centered flipped classroom environments. Educators should bring about conducive environments for effective pedagogy employment by offering choices, explaining rationales behind given tasks, and acknowledging student perspectives to nurture their motivation and self-regulated learning.

items.title: Teacher Professional Reasoning for AI-Mediated Language Teaching Under Multi-Level AI Governance: An Embedded Multiple-Case Study
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence is reshaping teaching, learning, assessment, and professional practice in English as a Foreign Language. However, little is known about how university teachers exercise professional reasoning within emerging AI governance environments. This embedded qualitative multiple-case study explored how university teachers of English as a Foreign Language in Vietnam reasoned professionally about generative artificial intelligence. The study combined semi-structured interviews with 13 teachers from 13 universities and an analysis of 88 policy and governance documents comprising 10 national, 7 ministerial, and 71 institutional documents. A documented search, screening, inventory, and staged coding procedure enabled the systematic identification, classification, and analysis of the document corpus. Interview and documentary data were analysed separately, first within cases and governance levels and then across cases using matrices and joint displays. Findings showed that teachers' professional reasoning was developed through continual negotiation between classroom realities and multi-level AI governance. Participants moved beyond their traditional roles as language experts to become learning designers, pedagogical facilitators, critical mentors, and ethical guides. They set context-appropriate boundaries for AI use, reframed ethics in terms of transparency and cognitive engagement, and adapted assessment to preserve evidence of student learning. The documents revealed a layered but uneven governance landscape. National strategies articulated broad directions; ministerial documents provided partial guidance; and institutional policies varied considerably. The integration of the two datasets showed that AI literacy, governance, assessment, ethics, and teacher agency were interconnected with teachers’ professional reasoning. The study proposed the governance-informed Identity-Agency-Ethics-Assessment Practices heuristic for understanding AI-mediated teacher professionalism.

items.title: Teachers’ technopedagogical competence and perspectives on artificial intelligence use in education
items.abstract: Digitalization has made technology-supported materials essential, yet their practical use remains inefficient. This study investigates the link between teachers’ technopedagogical competencies and their perspectives on integrating artificial intelligence (AI) into education. Using an explanatory sequential mixed-methods approach, research was conducted with 297 teachers in Gaziantep during the 2024–2025 academic year. Quantitative data was collected via an Intelligent TPACK framework scale, while qualitative insights were gathered through semi-structured interviews with 10 participants. Data analysis included t-tests, ANOVA, Scheffé post hoc tests, and content analysis. Results indicate that teachers' AI-related technopedagogical skills are at a low-to-moderate level. While gender showed no significant difference, variables such as age, seniority and prior experience with Web 2.0 or AI tools caused notable differences. Qualitatively, teachers reported using AI for instructional design, assessment efficiency, and professional development. However, concerns were raised regarding data security, overreliance, and the lack of emotional depth in AI interactions. Ultimately, the study concludes that AI should serve as a complementary tool rather than a replacement for teachers.

items.title: Ten pillars for responsible and ethical AI adoption in Lebanon’s health sector
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly integrated into healthcare systems globally, including diagnostics, predictive analytics, and public health surveillance. AI adoption is increasing, yet fragile and resource-limited settings face distinct ethical and legal challenges. Lebanon provides a complex case: since 2019, the country has experienced economic collapse, workforce migration, rising non-communicable diseases, and sustained refugee influx, alongside rapid digital expansion. In 2026, the Ministry of Public Health launched the National Digital Health Transformation Strategy (2025–2030), recognizing AI as a potential lever to strengthen services and rebuild public trust. However, national ethical and legal standards specific to healthcare AI remain underdeveloped. In this perspective report, we present AI opportunities, legal gaps, and ethical risks within Lebanon’s fragmented public–private system. AI offers potential benefits in clinical decision support, public health surveillance, workforce support, and medical education. Yet algorithmic bias, data protection weaknesses, regulatory ambiguity, and unclear liability expose patients and professionals to uncertainty. Lebanon currently operates within a regulatory gray zone, as existing healthcare system and data laws predate machine-learning-based decision systems. Drawing on international ethical frameworks and pluralistic moral traditions, we propose an ethical containment strategy grounded in human dignity, accountability, transparency, and equity. We outline ten pillars, including human-led decision-making, sector-specific governance within the Ministry of Public Health (MOPH), bias containment, strengthened data protection and cybersecurity, clarified legal responsibility, professional training, participatory oversight, and lifecycle evaluation. Ethical containment does not resist innovation; rather, it seeks to ensure that AI strengthens resilience and trust instead of amplifying systematic vulnerabilities. The credibility and acceptance of AI in Lebanon will depend more on the strength of its ethical and institutional frameworks than on the sophistication of the technology itself.

items.title: The AI crisis for teaching: "Train your own neural network!"
items.abstract: Everyone seems to be thinking about so-called artificial intelligence (AI) these days. As scientists, we understand that we're not about to have a conscious computer intelligence taking over the world, but we're nevertheless concerned about how "large language models" (LLMs) and AI "agents" are impacting the way that we do science. This concern has generated several recent essays about the effects of AI on research, including in my own field of astronomy and astrophysics. These opinion pieces tend to miss the biggest current concern for those whose jobs combine teaching with research - although the threat to future scientific research as we know it is probably a bit concerning, the effect on teaching is an existential crisis right now! We need to hang on to the parts of education that we think are at its core - so that students coming out of degree programmes are actually able to think for themselves, "like an astrophysicist". This means emphasising to students that they should use AI tools to support their education and not to replace it. One way of explaining the importance of this principle is to point out that students should be training their own neural networks.

items.title: The AI Efficiency Trap: Why Local Automation Gains Fail to Become Organizational Value
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence can deliver substantial task-level efficiency gains without generating equivalent organizational value. This Research Note conceptualizes this disconnect as the AI efficiency trap and introduces conversion loss as the mechanism through which local gains dissipate across organizational value flows. Four forms of conversion loss are identified: coordination, continuity, verification, and governance loss. Building on research on IT business value, digital transformation, AI capability, omnichannel integration, and human–AI collaboration, the paper develops a value-conversion framework. It argues that organizational complementarity, task-appropriate omnichannel integration, human–AI task fit, and end-to-end outcome feedback determine whether AI-enabled efficiencies survive their transmission into customer, business, and risk outcomes. The framework shifts attention from AI adoption toward the organizational conditions required for value realization at scale.

items.title: The Associations of Self-Determination and Cognitive Engagement with Vocational Students’ Critical Thinking Skills in a Gamified Learning Environment
items.abstract: A substantial body of previous research has examined gamification in educational settings, particularly its associations with self-determination, cognitive engagement, and critical thinking skills. However, there remain limitations in the analysis of gamification in relation to these constructs within vocational education. Therefore, this study was conducted to investigate the relationships among self-determination, cognitive engagement, and critical thinking skills in a learning process that incorporates gamification elements. A total of 309 students participated in this research and provided the data. The analysis was carried out using SmartPLS 3, applying Structural Equation Modelling (SEM) and Importance–Performance Map Analysis (IPMA). Based on the analytical results, there is a positive and significant relationship between self-determination and cognitive engagement. Furthermore, self-determination and cognitive engagement were positively associated with critical thinking skills. However, this study has limitations that should be acknowledged, as the data were obtained through self-report measures, which are subject to subjectivity and potential response bias. Therefore, future research is recommended to strengthen methodological rigor, both in terms of data collection and research approach, such as through qualitative studies and mixed-method designs.

items.title: THE COMPLEXITY GAP: AI IN STRATEGIC HCM
items.abstract: The transition from traditional Personnel Administration to Strategic Human Capital Management (HCM) redefines human assets from operational costs to the primary source of sustainable competitive advantage. However, executing this strategic vision in a post-pandemic environment presents unprecedented challenges. This theoretical paper systematically reflects upon the literature mapping the evolution of HCM. It applies the Resource-Based View (RBV) and the VRIO framework to analyze the synergistic impact of modern trends: Employee Experience (EX), organizational agility, continuous learning, and inclusion. The conceptual synthesis reveals that implementing these modern HCM imperatives creates a systemic "complexity gap." Organizations face a limitation of scalability, where the cognitive and analytical capacities of traditional management are overwhelmed by the need for hyper-personalization and massive data volumes. Artificial Intelligence (AI) is identified as a theoretical necessity rather than a mere technological upgrade. AI systems provide the augmented intelligence required to bridge the complexity gap. However, the paper critically highlights that this integration must navigate significant ethical risks, including algorithmic bias and privacy concerns, to ensure sustainable human-AI symbiosis.

items.title: The duality of playful work design: A diary study of designing fun and competition
items.abstract: Although employees often have limited control over task assignments, schedules, or collaboration partners, they may still have discretion in how they carry out tasks. Building on Job Demands-Resources theory, we integrate information-processing perspectives of play to propose that playful work design – proactively adding elements of fun and competition to routine activities – can be useful even in tightly structured jobs by increasing activated positive affect and reducing exhaustion. We tested this proposition in a 20-day diary study among 57 Norwegian naval cadets, yielding 1,046 day-level observations, using multilevel structural equation modeling. On days when cadets designed their work playfully, they reported more activated positive affect and less exhaustion. Combining designing fun with designing competition amplified these benefits. Thus, small discretionary choices in how employees approach work may produce immediate well-being gains in low-discretion roles and offer a micro-level pathway through which play at work can support performance.

items.title: The Impact of Artificial Intelligence on Different Aspects of the Society
items.abstract: Abstract In recent times, artificial intelligence (AI) is emerging as a revolutionary transformative force in various sectors of the contemporary society. It has rapidly becomes an integral part of our daily lives. Now a days AI plays crucial role in transforming various aspects of society and generate new possibilities and opportunities. The paper also present a dissection of an impact of AI on different aspects of the society including agriculture, industry, education, market, finance, business, transportation, employment, healthcare etc. This article is presented in a narrative review. The main object of this research paper is an attempt to find and to analyze the positive and negative impact of artificial intelligence on various field of the society. This research paper provides a comprehensive overview of the impact of AI on various aspects of the society in the form of dynamic nature of economy, transformation in education system, modern and advanced healthcare system, change in nature of employment and ethics etc. The collected literature for this research paper is focused on socio-economic influence as well as future fear and challenges in implementing of AI. The AI related literature shows that it has large potential to provide significant benefits for the present modern society but it has also aware us about challenges and risk in implementing of AI technology. Because of many scientists, technologists and others concerned with the welfare of society have started fearing about the extensive use of AI and its impacts on the society. The medical field is more affected by use of AI technology. It plays a crucial role in diagnosis, surgery, appropriate treatment methods and other related healthcare services. It can also play an important role in education transforming with student personalized learning experience for student and teacher also. However, we cannot ignore some problems about using of AI in the field of viability of employment, economic inequality, and ethical issues. In short, this research paper provides a comprehensive overview of the impact of AI on various aspects of the present society life.

items.title: The Impact of Organizational Ergonomics on Job Burnout: Evidence from Higher Education Institutions in Iraq
items.abstract: This research aims to examine organizational ergonomics and its impact on job burnout among a random sample of teaching and administrative staff employed at universities, colleges, and institutes within higher education institutions in Iraq. This topic is of considerable importance because improving organizational ergonomics can enhance the work environment, increase job performance, and promote employee well-being. The research also seeks to address the problem of occupational stress and excessive workloads resulting from increasing teaching and administrative tasks assigned to employees in higher education institutions. These pressures contribute to higher levels of job burnout and adversely affect employee performance and job satisfaction. A descriptive-analytical approach was adopted, and data were collected using a structured questionnaire administered to a random sample of teaching and administrative staff. A total of 108 valid questionnaires. The data were analyzed using the Statistical Package for the Social Sciences (SPSS) and the Analysis of Moment Structures (AMOS) program. The results showed a statistically significant positive correlation and influence between the two variables. This finding contradicts the prevailing theoretical trend in the literature. This result suggests the possibility of other organizational or psychological factors influencing this relationship within Iraqi higher education institutions. Accordingly, the study recommends that decision-makers in Iraqi higher education institutions should move beyond the mere implementation of ergonomic practices and adopt a comprehensive approach that integrates improvements to the physical work environment with psychological and social support, while proactively managing employee expectations to reduce job burnout and enhance organizational effectiveness.

items.title: The Legal and Ethical Challenges of Using Artificial Intelligence in Algeria
items.abstract: This study explores the legal and ethical problems arising from the integration of artificial intelligence technologies into the administrative and public-service systems of Algeria. It asks how far the country's existing legislative arsenal and its rules of digital ethics can absorb the accelerating development of intelligent systems, and assesses the role of the existing digital infrastructure in securing that transition. The paper adopts a descriptive-analytical methodology: the descriptive component inventories the relevant legal instruments and the available technical capacity, while the analytical component performs a gap analysis of whether texts drafted for classical digitisation can accommodate concepts such as the legal personality of a robot or liability for an algorithmic act, and subjects current digital administrative practice to critique against international ethical standards of transparency, fairness and non-discrimination. The study concludes that there is a clear legislative gap in the attribution of legal responsibility for algorithmic acts, particularly under the personal data protection legislation, because Algerian civil and criminal liability alike presuppose a discerning, willing human author whom an autonomous and opaque system does not supply. It further finds that the digital infrastructure, and specifically data centres and the national cloud, is the cornerstone of digital sovereignty and of ethical privacy, provided it is reinforced by an advanced cybersecurity framework and by reduced dependence on closed foreign platforms. The study recommends the drafting of a dedicated national legal framework and ethical charter for artificial intelligence, balancing technological innovation against the protection of the fundamental rights of the Algerian citizen.
